Durable hash-bound transition intent reserves one successor. Successor checkpoint pin precedes the atomic output pin commit. Only identical explicit activation may resume; constructors do not finish partial activation. Partial staging files and lost commit acknowledgement are covered.

Historical policy snapshots, checkpoint pins and ledger hashes form an explicit predecessor chain; historical DBs are opened read-only. Status/result use the owning policy allowance and the current original research reader.

Historical request identity is checked before the successor ledger: same fingerprint reuses, changed content returns 409, broken history returns 503 without accepting a new task. Submit and dispatch check current activation; superseded workers do not send or rewrite the old ledger.
hash_semantics: Expected predecessor hash is the canonical policy.sha256 already exposed by status/pin. Transition receipts additionally bind both policy source paths and their exact byte SHA256. CLI invocation does not grant authorization or modify environment/service configuration.
